entities.summary: Agnes of Aquitaine, Queen of Aragon and Navarre, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval landscape. Born around 1122, she married Alfonso I of Aragon and later King Sancho II of Navarre, solidifying her position as a powerful queen consort. Her influence extended beyond her marriages, as she patronized the arts and supported the establishment of the University of Bologna. As a result, her legacy has been immortalized in the works of medieval chroniclers, who praised her intelligence, beauty, and strong will. Despite the limited availability of her personal life, Agnes of Aquitaine remains a significant figure in the annals of medieval history, embodying the resilience and determination of women in a patriarchal society.
